One of the twelve apostles, called Thaddaeus or Judas son of James. He asked Jesus a question during the farewell discourse.
Recognition of what has been received. The psalms invite us to give thanks to the LORD "for he is good", and Paul recommends giving thanks in everything.

Seven men chosen by the church in Jerusalem to oversee the distribution to the needy: Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas and Nicolaus. Stephen and Philip also stood out in preaching.

Group of the twelve disciples whom Jesus chose, linked to the twelve tribes of Israel. The list: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot, replaced by Matthias.
Great city of Upper Egypt, mentioned by Nahum as an example of a powerful city that was also destroyed.
Port city of Macedonia, to which Paul wrote two letters.
One of the twelve apostles, also called Didymus, "twin". He doubted the resurrection until he saw Jesus and then declared: "My Lord and my God!"
Plants that grew in the ground as a consequence of the fall. Jesus used them in the parable of the sower, and a crown of them was placed on his head.

Flat ground where grain was threshed, separating the kernel from the chaff in the wind. David bought the threshing floor of Araunah, where the temple was built. John the Baptist uses the image in his preaching.
City in Asia, home of Lydia, the seller of purple. Seat of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
City founded by Herod Antipas on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, in honor of the emperor Tiberius. The Sea of Galilee is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
King of Assyria who took territories of northern Israel and carried off captives, in the time of Pekah and of Ahaz.
One of the rivers of Eden, which runs east of Assyria; Daniel had a vision on its banks.
Young disciple from Lystra, son of a Jewish mother and a Greek father, companion of Paul and recipient of two pastoral letters.
King of Cush (Ethiopia) who marched against Sennacherib in the time of Hezekiah.
Tenth part of the produce or income, given to God. In the law, it supported the Levites and the needy. Abraham had already given it to the priest Melchizedek.
Greek co-worker of Paul, sent to Corinth and to Crete. One of the pastoral letters is addressed to him.
Opponent of Nehemiah, ally of Sanballat, who mocked the rebuilding of the walls and tried to intimidate him.

Speech inspired by the Spirit. At Pentecost, the disciples spoke in tongues that each of those present understood. In Corinth, Paul regulates the use of tongues in the assembly, which were to be interpreted.
Hebrew word for "instruction" or "law". It designates the first five books of the Bible, also called the Pentateuch, and in a broader sense all the teaching given by God to Israel.
Episode in which Jesus changed in appearance before Peter, James and John, on a high mountain, and Moses and Elijah appeared talking with him.

Tree in the middle of the garden of Eden, from whose fruit Adam and Eve were prevented from eating after the fall. It appears in Proverbs as an image of wisdom and reappears in Revelation, in the new creation.

Intense distress and suffering. Jesus says that in the world we will have tribulation, but that he has overcome the world. In Matthew and Revelation, "great tribulation" appears as a time of trial before the end.

Theological term, which does not appear in the Bible, used by the Christian tradition to sum up what is understood from the biblical witness about Father, Son and Holy Spirit as one God. Matthew's baptismal formula and the greetings of the letters are often cited.
Entry of Jesus into Jerusalem riding on a colt, acclaimed with branches and shouts of "Hosanna", fulfilling Zechariah's prophecy of the humble king.
Port of Asia Minor, where Paul had the vision of the Macedonian and later raised Eutychus.
Gentile Christian of Ephesus. His presence with Paul in Jerusalem gave occasion for the riot that led to the apostle's arrest.
Wind instrument made from a ram's horn, used to call the people, warn of danger and mark feasts. The walls of Jericho fell at the sound of trumpets. In Revelation, angels blow seven trumpets.
The Bible presents it as the faithfulness of God and as what is real. Jesus says of himself: "I am the way, the truth, and the life", and promises that the truth "will make you free".

The twelve groups descended from the sons of Jacob: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph (Ephraim and Manasseh) and Benjamin. Jesus chose twelve apostles, echoing the twelve tribes.

Parable of a father who asks two sons to work in the vineyard: one says no and goes, the other says yes and does not go. Jesus applies it to tax collectors and prostitutes who believe, and to the leaders who do not.
Companion of Paul, from the province of Asia, bearer of letters and called "the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord".
Phoenician coastal cities, famous for maritime trade. Jesus mentioned both when speaking of cities that would have repented if they had seen his miracles.

Lack of faith. It appears as an obstacle to God's action, as in Nazareth, where Jesus "could do no mighty work" because of their unbelief. Thomas is remembered for being told to "be not faithless, but believing".
Parable of the servant forgiven a great debt who refuses to forgive a small debt of a fellow servant. It teaches that whoever has been forgiven must forgive.
State of being united. Jesus prayed that his disciples would be one, and Paul says that the church must keep "the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace".
Parable of the widow who keeps pleading with an unjust judge until she gets justice. Jesus uses it to teach us always to pray and not to lose heart.
Parable of the manager who, about to be dismissed, uses his master's money to make friends. Jesus praises his shrewdness and teaches about the use of possessions.
Room on the upper floor of a house in Jerusalem, prepared for the last supper of Jesus with the disciples and where they gathered after the ascension.
Ancient city of Mesopotamia, near the Euphrates, from which Abraham left with his family.
Hittite soldier in David's army and husband of Bathsheba, sent to the front of the battle to die.
Prophet who announced judgment on Jerusalem in the time of Jehoiakim and was executed by the king. Not to be confused with Uriah the Hittite.
Objects kept in the breastplate of the high priest, used to consult the will of God. Their exact form is unknown.
Man who died when touching the ark of the covenant as it was being transported, an episode that recalls the reverence due to God's holiness.

King of Judah for fifty-two years, prosperous and strong, but who grew proud and wanted to offer incense in the temple, and was struck with leprosy. In the year of Uzziah's death, Isaiah had the vision of the Lord in the temple.
Valley near Jericho, where Achan was stoned. The prophets promise that it will become a "door of hope."
Vision of Ezekiel of a valley full of bones that come to life by the word and the breath of God, an image of the restoration of Israel after the exile.
Valley where the armies of Israel and the Philistines faced each other, and where David killed Goliath.
Symbolic name, in Joel, for the place of God's judgment on the nations. Tradition associates it with the Kidron valley, in Jerusalem.
In Ecclesiastes, "vanity" translates a term that means "breath", or what passes and has no substance, and the book repeats it. It also means pride or futility.
Queen of Persia, wife of Ahasuerus, who refused to appear at the king's banquet and was deposed, opening the way for Esther to become queen.
Curtain that separated the holy place from the most holy. The gospels say it was torn from top to bottom when Jesus died. Hebrews sees in this the opening of the way to God.
Plantation of grapes, one of the most used images for God's people. Isaiah sings of the unfruitful vineyard; Jesus says: "I am the true vine".

Young woman who has not had sexual relations. Isaiah announces that a young woman will conceive Immanuel, and Matthew and Luke see the fulfillment in Mary. Christians differ on other aspects of the doctrine about Mary.

Experience in which God shows something to someone, common in the prophets and in Revelation. It is also the capacity to see. "Where there is no vision, the people perish" (Prov 29:18), in some translations.
Visit of Mary to Elizabeth, who greeted her as "the mother of my Lord". Mary responded with the song that tradition calls the Magnificat.
Solemn promise made to God. The law regulates vows and warns against failing to keep them. Jesus teaches us to be sincere, so that our "yes" is "yes" and our "no" is "no".
Translation of the Bible into Latin made by Jerome, at the end of the 4th century. For centuries it was the standard text of the church in the West.
Each of the divisions of the night, for sentinel duty. The Jews had three, and the Romans four. The gospels mention the "fourth watch" of the night.
Attention and readiness. Jesus teaches us to watch because we do not know the day or the hour of his return, and Paul and Peter ask for sobriety and watchfulness. See also the night watches.
Wedding in Cana of Galilee at which Jesus turned water into wine, the first of the "signs" in John's Gospel.
Basic cereal for bread. Jesus compares his own death to the grain of wheat that falls into the earth and bears much fruit.
Parable in which an enemy sows darnel among the wheat. The owner orders them to wait for the harvest to separate one from the other, teaching patience in the face of evil until the final judgment.
Parable of the owner of the vineyard whose tenants mistreat the servants and kill the son. Jesus addressed it to the leaders of Israel, and cited the rejected stone that becomes the cornerstone.

In Israel, widows and orphans were the most vulnerable, and the law and the prophets command that they be cared for. Jesus praised the poor widow who gave all she had, and the early church organized care for widows.
Two small copper coins that a poor widow put into the temple offering box and that Jesus valued more than the offerings of the rich.
Arid region east of Jerusalem, descending toward the Dead Sea, where John the Baptist preached and Jesus was tempted.
Drink made from the grape, present at meals and feasts. It is a symbol of joy and also of drunkenness, which the Bible condemns. Jesus turned water into wine and took the cup at the Supper.
Structure where grapes or olives were trodden to make wine and oil. The prophets use the winepress as an image of judgment. Gethsemane means "oil press".
Container of animal hide, for storing wine or water. Jesus said that new wine is not put into old wineskins.
Skill in living well before God. The wisdom books are Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and Song of Solomon. "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom."
One who has seen or heard something and declares it. Jesus told the disciples they would be his witnesses to the ends of the earth. "Martyr" comes from the Greek for "witness".
Predator of sheep, an image of false teachers and persecutors. Isaiah announces a time when the wolf will live with the lamb.
Vision of Revelation of a woman crowned with stars who gives birth to a son and is pursued by a great dragon, identified as the ancient serpent, the devil.
Woman with a flow of blood
Woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years and was healed by touching the edge of Jesus' cloak. He called her "daughter" and said: "Your faith has made you well".
Woman with the issue of blood
Fiber of sheep, used in clothing. Isaiah says that sins, though red like crimson, will become white as wool.

Expression for God's message to human beings. In the Bible, the word of God creates the world, is spoken by the prophets, is embodied in Jesus and is proclaimed by the church. Today it also designates the Scriptures.

In the Bible, part of the human calling even before the fall, which afterwards became burdensome. Paul commands those who can work to work with their own hands, and Jesus says that the Father "is still working".
Parable of the owner of a vineyard who pays the same wage to workers hired at different hours, teaching that God's grace does not follow the logic of merit.
In the Bible, it can mean creation, humanity or, in John and Paul, the order that opposes God. John says that God so loved the world that he gave his Son, and also warns against loving the world.
Recognition of God's greatness and holiness in attitude, word and life. The Bible speaks of worshiping "in spirit and truth" and of offering one's own body as a living sacrifice.

Act of worshiping God, in a gathering or in daily life. In the Old Testament, it was tied to the temple, priests and sacrifices. In the New Testament, the gathering of Christians includes prayer, teaching, songs and the Supper.

Holy response of God to evil and injustice. In the prophets, it is the counterpart of his love. Paul says that the wrath of God is revealed against all ungodliness and that Christ rescues us from the wrath to come.

Episode of the banquet of Belshazzar, in which a hand wrote on the wall "Mene, Mene, Tekel, Parsin". Daniel interpreted it as the end of the kingdom. From it comes the expression "the writing on the wall".

Personal name of God in Hebrew, made up of four consonants (YHWH). Out of respect, the Jews stopped pronouncing it, reading "Adonai" instead. Many translations render it "LORD", in capital letters. It is linked to "I AM WHO I AM".
Piece of wood that joined draft animals. In the Bible it is an image of labor, of oppression or of teaching. Jesus invites: "Take my yoke upon you".
Chief tax collector in Jericho, short in stature, who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, received him at home and promised to repay what he had taken.
Priest in David's time, who remained faithful to him in Absalom's revolt and anointed Solomon king. He became high priest in Solomon's reign, and his line came to serve the temple.
Phoenician city near Sidon, where Elijah was hosted by a widow and multiplied the flour and oil.
Intense dedication and ardor for a cause. The Bible speaks of God's zeal for his people and of zeal for God. Paul acknowledges that the Jews have "a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge".
Jewish resistance movement against Roman rule. One of the apostles, Simon, was called "the Zealot".
Fisherman of Galilee, father of the apostles James and John. He had hired servants and a boat, and his sons left the boat and their father to follow Jesus.

Tenth son of Jacob, sixth of Leah. The tribe occupied land between the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean. The Galilee of Jesus' time corresponds in large part to the territories of Zebulun and Naphtali.

Name of several figures. The best known in the New Testament is the priest of Herod's time, father of John the Baptist, who was struck mute for not believing the angel's announcement and recovered his speech when he named his son; his song is called the Benedictus. In the Old Testament there is also the prophet Zechariah, from the period after the exile, who encourages the rebuilding of the temple and announces a humble king riding on a donkey.
Last king of Judah, put on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar, against whom he rebelled. Jerusalem was destroyed in 586 BC, his sons were killed before him and he was blinded and taken captive.
Israelite of the tribe of Manasseh who died without sons. His five daughters asked for their father's inheritance, and the law was adjusted so that daughters could inherit.
Prophet of Judah in the time of King Josiah, who announced "the day of the Lord" and the restoration of a humble remnant.
Jewish leader who, with the high priest Joshua, led the return from exile and the rebuilding of the temple.
Greek gods whom the people of Lystra thought they saw in Barnabas and Paul on seeing the miracle. They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, and Paul stopped them from offering sacrifices to them.
Servant of the house of Saul who told David about Mephibosheth and later falsely accused him of disloyalty.
Originally the fortified hill of Jerusalem conquered by David. It came to mean the temple mount, the city and the people of God.
Wife of Moses, daughter of Jethro, the priest of Midian.
